summary: Capture the CoCo Zero vision in the user's own words (docs/vision.md)
description: Every other document derives from this, so it goes first. Interview the user and write docs/vision.md: why CoCo Zero exists, who it is for, what it is not. Established so far from the reference project (~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero (github.com/ugufru/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero)): it began as XRoar on a Waveshare RP2350-PiZero, a CoCo 2 on a 65 x 30 mm board with picture and sound over one digital video cable at 60 fps, USB keyboard and gamepad, microSD; it now also runs a 128 KB CoCo 3; its CLAUDE.md rule 'improvements are on by default, authentic behaviour stays available'; PIZERO-176's 'CoCo Zero is like a little playground for developers, and our limits do not always need to be practical if they are within reach'; units are given away, not sold (docs/kit.md). OPEN QUESTIONS to settle with the user: (1) is CoCo Zero a product, a machine, or a standard any board can meet; (2) does the name cover only RP2350 boards, or also the other XRoar ports in ~/github (Fruit Jam, RP2350-43B, AMOLED, 1.44in LCD HAT); (3) is the cocozero machine profile (CZ-5) the heart of the identity, or the hardware; (4) the document license (e.g. CC BY-SA 4.0) and whether implementations must be open source like XRoar (GPL); (5) the intended audience: builders, developers writing software for it, or both. DONE WHEN: the user has read vision.md and agrees it says what they mean. [2026-10-21 Settled with the user: CoCo Zero is a form factor plus a small feature set, not one board. As every CoCo 2 variant (including the Korean-built ones) shared one motherboard size and case, every CoCo Zero shares the Raspberry Pi Zero board size; the 'Zero' names that size, used by Raspberry Pi, Waveshare, Orange Pi and others. Features: the user named USB-C, mini HDMI and microSD as the ones that stand out and does not want the spec too specific. This answers open questions 1 and 2 (any Pi Zero size board can qualify) and largely 3 (the form factor is the identity; the machine profile is secondary). Still open: 4 (licenses), 5 (audience).] [2026-10-21 Second meaning of 'Zero', from the user: bare metal. Zero operating system in the way, only a lightweight monitor and configuration screen that runs nothing else: just you and the machine, with one layer of software between. Approximated as closely as possible while keeping the essence of operating a CoCo. The user will deepen this later (CZ-18). Also from the user: a CoCo Zero emulates a CoCo 1, 2 or 3 (128K, ideally 512K, 2M and more) (CZ-19), and does extra things the original CoCos never did, a list that will grow (CZ-12). So the vision page has three pillars: the Pi Zero form factor, bare metal, and the CoCo plus extras.] [2026-10-21 The user's model for this repo (2026-10-21): the main documentation is very sparse. It does not tell you how to build a CoCo Zero beyond the general shape. Think of the rules for a kei car or a US mailbox, or a computer case standard: it leaves the most room for DIY builders to adapt it and make it what they want, while letting them depend on third-party manufacturers for the electronics. This is the governing rule for every spec page and belongs at the top of the vision page.] [2026-10-21 The README now states the vision in short form (CZ-1). docs/vision.md may not be needed at all: decide with the user whether the README section is enough.] [2026-10-25 Closed with the user's agreement: the README's 'The vision' section is the vision statement, and docs/vision.md is not being written. Questions 1 to 3 were settled earlier. Remainder filed: question 4 (document license, and whether implementations must be open source) goes to CZ-22 with LICENSE; question 5 (intended audience) is CZ-23.]

summary: Performance and machine requirements are absolute or untestable
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). spec/features.md:29-32 and spec/machines.md. (a) 'No dropped frames' and 'No gaps in the sound' have no conditions or measure; 'dropped' could mean DVI output frames or emulated frames. The reference pauses the machine and fades sound for the configuration overlay (src/main.cpp around 606 and 1033), pauses about a second for a screenshot, and restarts when switching to the CoCo 3. Scope it to 'while the emulated CoCo runs' and say which frames. (b) 'Runs in real time at double speed' could mean always 1.79 MHz (which breaks timing-sensitive software) or keeps up when software selects it; say which, whether it applies to an offered CoCo 1 or 2, and whether 60.00 vs 59.94 Hz pacing matters. (c) 'Power-on goes straight to the BASIC prompt' cannot happen with no ROMs, and no CoCo Zero ships with them; write 'given the owner's ROMs', and decide whether 'ships without ROMs' is a requirement or guidance (README.md:137 states it as fact). (d) 'Emulates a CoCo 3' has no minimum; consider 'boots Super Extended Color BASIC from an owner-supplied ROM with 128K visible'. Keep the sparse-spec model (principle 1): few lines, testable. DONE WHEN: two honest builders would agree whether a build meets each line. [2026-10-26 User: this is spec. The performance lines stay in the one-page spec; the work is wording them concisely and testably, not removing them.]

summary: USB device requirements: name a baseline instead of 'works'
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). spec/features.md:15-20 reads to a user as 'every keyboard, gamepad, hub and USB audio device works'. The reference meets narrower terms: a keyboard plugged straight into the board must be present at power-on; the port is full speed only; the tested gamepad's Switch mode sends nothing; USB audio needs UAC1 or UAC2, 16-bit 48 kHz, present at power-on (reference docs/sound.md:328). Also: 'a simple USB hub (one with a single hub chip)' is not checkable by a buyer; 'works as the CoCo's joysticks' does not say whether one gamepad covers both joysticks and both buttons; 'a standard USB-C keyboard' leaves out USB-A keyboards on an adapter, which the reference supports. DO: rewrite as a named baseline (for example HID boot keyboard, a HID gamepad, UAC1 at 48 kHz, present at power-on) or 'at least one ...'. DONE WHEN: the reference meets the USB lines as written and a buyer can tell what to expect. [2026-10-26 User: 'works' is not vague: if USB did not work, nothing plugged into it would be accessible. USB must support a hub, a keyboard, a generic USB game controller, and class-compliant USB audio. Class-compliant USB MIDI is a strong candidate to add (filed as CZ-40). A mouse is an obvious choice but would need a GUI to justify it, which there is not yet. Remaining from the review for discussion: devices present only at power-on, USB-C vs USB-A keyboards on an adapter, and the 'single hub chip' wording.]

summary: Define 'open source' and where a library ends and an OS begins
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). (a) spec/features.md:40 'The firmware is open source' has no license test (source-available or non-commercial?) and no scope (bootloader, closed boot blobs, co-processor or HAT firmware). A Pi Zero-class build boots through closed VideoCore firmware. Name a test, for example an OSI-approved license for everything the builder writes or links, and say how closed vendor boot code is treated. README.md:84 'XRoar is GPL 3, so its source travels with it' is wrong: the GPL puts a duty on whoever distributes binaries; fix the sentence. (b) spec/zero-os.md:8-9 allows 'a library the firmware is built on'. FreeRTOS, Zephyr, NuttX and ChibiOS are statically linked libraries with schedulers, so builders will disagree on them. CZ-26 settled the wording deliberately; this reopens only the gap. Consider naming the disqualifying traits (processes, a shell, loading programs other than the emulator) and saying which processor the rule applies to (a VideoCore or a Linux HAT). DONE WHEN: a builder can tell from the text whether their license and their RTOS are allowed. [2026-10-26 User: this is spec. Open source stays a requirement; the work is defining it concisely.]

summary: Configuration screen: exhaustive list or examples, and the 'monitor'
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). spec/zero-os.md:10-15: 'one configuration screen. It may: ...' does not say whether the list is all that is allowed or examples, and since every item is 'may', a screen that does nothing conforms. The reference has several lists (disks, programs, cartridges, files), an INFO page and a settings editor (reference README:159-163), more than 'one screen'. Screenshots, logging to the card and volume keys are neither listed nor clearly 'nothing else'. README.md:47 promises 'a lightweight monitor', which the spec never mentions; a builder cannot tell whether a 6809 machine-language monitor is allowed. DO: say 'one configuration interface', state whether the list is exhaustive, cover small firmware functions like screenshots, and either add the monitor or drop it from the README. Keep docs/glossary.md 'Configuration screen' in step. DONE WHEN: the reference's interface plainly conforms. [2026-10-26 User: the configuration screen is very loose and open to the builder's preferences, but still necessary. In practical terms it must let you assign DSK images. The other items (emulator options, system information, loading programs and cartridges directly) are not critical; the reference exceeds the spec here. Direction: make assigning disk images the one required function and leave the rest to the builder.] [2026-10-26 Done per the user's direction: spec/zero-os.md now says the configuration screen 'mounts disk images. It may also:' set the emulator's options, show system information, load programs and cartridges directly. The status line cites CZ-36 and the PDF is rebuilt, still one page. docs/extras.md lists mounting disks under 'On every CoCo Zero'. Not decided: whether 'one screen' should read 'one interface' (the reference has several lists and pages), and whether small functions such as screenshots and the README's 'lightweight monitor' count as 'nothing else'.] [2026-10-26 Left as is by decision: 'one configuration screen' reads as one place for configuration however many pages it has, and 'runs nothing else' means no other programs, not no firmware features such as screenshots. The area is deliberately loose and up to the builder. No follow-up filed. Closed at the user's request.]

summary: Video, sound and connectors: precise enough for TVs and builders
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). (a) spec/features.md:24-25: DVI carries no audio by itself; embedding sound needs HDMI-style data islands and InfoFrames, and some TVs mute audio without them. Describe it in neutral terms (TMDS video with 2-channel L-PCM audio packets as consumer TVs accept, possibly citing CTA-861) without using the licensed HDMI name for the signal (CZ-25). Say whether 640 x 480 is the minimum or the only mode, and whether 59.94 Hz counts as 60. (b) spec/features.md:7-11: say whether ports are 'at least' (CZ-16 meant at least) and must be on the board (adapters and pigtails, such as micro USB to USB-C on a Pi Zero 2 W); define what 'programming' must allow. (c) Region: 60 Hz output implies NTSC; say the emulated machine is NTSC, or that region is the builder's choice. Keyboard mapping of BREAK, CLEAR and @ can stay open but could be said. DONE WHEN: a build that meets the text works with sound on an ordinary TV. [2026-10-26 User: this is clear as it stands. DVI with embedded audio over a mini HDMI connector, to any monitor that supports 640 x 480 at 60 Hz. Compatibility is the monitor's responsibility, and not all TVs and monitors will be compatible; with the signal identified, there is a good chance of connecting easily. Likely closes with no change to the signal wording.]

summary: Versions and the name: changelog, tags, registry column, near-miss wording
description: From the compliance review of 2026-10-26 (a read-only review of the whole repo from the point of view of other builders and users; findings checked against the files). (a) docs/versioning.md defines MAJOR.MINOR and the history was applied consistently (1.0 CZ-11, 2.0 CZ-29, 2.1 CZ-26), but there is no changelog and no git tags; version 1.0 exists only in git history. Page status lines cite issues, not versions. implementations/README.md has no version column (CZ-9 left it out before versions existed). Nothing says whether a build that met 1.0 keeps the name after 2.0. Add a short changelog, a tag per version, a version column, and a line on keeping the name. (b) docs/name.md: 'There is no CoCo Zero compatible' sits next to 'can say which version it follows and what it leaves out'. Give the allowed wording for a near miss, and say the standard meant is the one at github.com/ugufru/coco-zero (CC BY 4.0 lets anyone publish a modified copy). Whether 'CoCo' is a protected mark is unchecked; a trademark search would settle it. DONE WHEN: a builder can state which version they meet and how to describe a near miss. [2026-10-26 User: the spec is version 1.0 and stays 1.0 until the CoCo Zero is released as a product. Done: docs/versioning.md now says current version 1.0, that it may change without a new number until the first release, and that MAJOR.MINOR numbering applies after it; README says version 1.0; the PDF header reads 1.0. The 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 bumps recorded in CZ-29, CZ-26 and CZ-31 no longer stand. The changelog, tags and registry version column wait for the release. The near-miss naming wording in docs/name.md remains.] [2026-10-26 Naming done along the rule docs/name.md already stated (no half-way names): the sentence letting a near miss 'say which version it follows and what it leaves out' was removed, since it contradicted that rule. 'Meets every requirement' now points at the one-page spec, and the page says the standard is the one published at github.com/ugufru/coco-zero. The trademark search on 'CoCo' was not done and is not planned. With versioning settled earlier (1.0 until release), this is the substance of CZ-38; the changelog, tags and registry version column wait for the release.] [2026-10-26 Closed at the user's request.]

summary: Class-compliant USB MIDI as a requirement?
description: Raised by the user while discussing CZ-34 on 2026-10-26: class-compliant USB MIDI is a strong candidate to add to the USB requirements in spec/features.md, alongside the hub, keyboard, generic game controller and class-compliant audio. Not decided. To settle: what a CoCo Zero would do with MIDI (for example the CoCo MIDI paks and software that drove them), whether the reference firmware can support it, and the one-line requirement. A mouse was considered at the same time and set aside: it would need a GUI to justify it, which the CoCo Zero does not have.
